subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw mitigate Codex app-server's 10-second external-auth refresh callback locally, or wait for upstream Codex configurability while relying on adjacent auth-deadline and error-classification fixes?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable fix changes the Codex auth bridge contract: returning cached tokens, forcing every callback refresh, adding status/degraded guidance, or depending on upstream each has different compatibility and operator-impact tradeoffs.

options.title: Choose a local bridge mitigation
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and design a local OpenClaw fix so usable cached tokens or bounded refresh behavior can answer Codex callbacks inside the upstream 10-second deadline.

options.title: Defer to upstream configurability
options.body: Wait for upstream Codex to make the callback timeout configurable, while documenting that shipped OpenClaw runtimes can still fail on slow callback refreshes.

options.title: Route only adjacent work elsewhere
options.body: Treat stale external fallback, runtime auth deadlock, and fallback classification as separate issues or PRs, but leave this issue open for the remaining callback deadline mismatch.

recommendation.title: Choose a local bridge mitigation
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and design a local OpenClaw fix so usable cached tokens or bounded refresh behavior can answer Codex callbacks inside the upstream 10-second deadline.

likelyOwner.reason: This account recently landed the overlapping OpenAI OAuth refresh-failure fix and added the latest production evidence, making it the best current routing signal for the next maintainer choice.
